title: Fire departments warn of risks involved with fireworks ahead of Fourth of July - NewsBreak
text: With Fourth of July just around the corner, fire departments are warning people about the potential risks that come with handling fireworks. Chief of Operations at Brookline Fire Protection District, Will Glenn, said that the week of July 4 is when most firework related injuries and accidents occur. “We’ll start seeing the uptick as people are getting closer to a holiday to put a number on, it would be really difficult just because, you know, accidents happen and sometimes are common and big number sometimes becomes small numbers, but accidents happen,” Glenn said. He said it’s important to have a water source nearby when handling fireworks to case they produce flames and start to spread. If you are transporting fireworks to or from a site, Glenn advises people to use vehicles like pickup trucks instead of enclosed vehicles like SUVs. Additionally, Brookline firefighter Keith Winchell said it’s important to watch your surroundings before igniting. “When we’re shooting our fireworks or putting them in safe directions, we’re not pointing them at people, animals,” Winchell said. “We’re not going to point out any flammable material.” Winchell adds that safety glasses are great ways to prevent any potential eye injuries when operating fireworks. According to Travis Trent, the Deputy Chief at Logan-Rogersville Fire Protection District, children are especially at risk from firework related injuries. “Make sure to watch the kids, pay attention to what they’re doing when they light a firecracker or any type of thing,” said Trent. “Make sure that they don’t go back. It doesn’t go off as fast as they think it should. It still could be lit and could blow up in close proximity and they can result in an injury.” Both Trent and Glenn warn that injuries sustained from fireworks could lead to permanent damage, such as severe burns or even loss of fingers or limbs. “You never know how much powder is loaded into them or if somebody is wire twisting the fuses together to make them bigger,” said Trent. “There’s always that always that possibility. And there could be potential to have some type of blast injuries that are not always associated with just fireworks.” For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to KOLR - OzarksFirst.com.
